pr_title: [wasm][debugger] Fix DebuggerTypeProxy for structs and for classes with multiple constructors
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/68390.
As a result of the discussion here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/75958#discussion_r995534127I I separated the test fix into this PR. `EvaluateBrowsableRootHidden` when run on main is failing, so the quoted PR changes are not connected with the problem.
The problem: `DebuggerProxy` was working only in a specific case - when the proxy class had only one constructor with 1 argument or the constructor we intended to use was declared as the first one. 
Fix:
- we are able to serve multiple constructors and recognise the proper one by number of arguments and their type.
- we support `DebuggerProxy` for value types (not only classes).

Connected issues:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/77315
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/77768

issue_context.title: [wasm][debugger] Add support for ValueTypes in DebuggerProxyAttribute
issue_context.body:
Runtime does not support invoking .ctor on ValueType. 

Reproduction: remove `return null` from `GetValuesFromDebuggerProxyAttribute` and uncomment //FIXME: Issue #68390
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/87645922fe4b493213c6d4d9dfc936ad9c9b47b5/src/mono/wasm/debugger/BrowserDebugProxy/MonoSDBHelper.cs#L2273
Run test: `DebuggerTests.EvaluateOnCallFrameTests.EvaluateBrowsableRootHidden` with Theory data: "EvaluateBrowsableStruct" to evaluate `testPropertiesNone.list`.

Behavior:
for properties Invoke of .ctor fails in the runtime. In this case we are sending a buffer with 7 fields: 
```
240 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 1 17 0 0 0 0 0 9 0 0 0 7 18 0 0 0 21 29 0 0 0 22 14 0 0 0 8 240 29 2 0 0 0 1 0 0 0 2 17 1 0 0 0 0 3 0 0 0 1 8 0 0 0 0 17 0 0 0 0 0 4 0 0 0 2 8 0 0 0 100 2 0 0 0 1 18 0 0 0 23
```
First error is caused by runtime not supporting type == MONO_TYPE_SZARRAY inside of valueTypes. Adding this option to default case in `decode_value_internal` helps to get to the remaining errors.

For fields we are sending a buffer with 2 fields:
```
240 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 1 17 0 0 0 0 0 3 0 0 0 2 8 0 0 0 100 2 0 0 0 1
```
Invoke .ctor in fields returns an object of a collection type. While getting its members in `GetTypeMemberValues` we are calling InvokeMethod again, in `GetNonAutomaticPropertyValues` which results in another runtime exception.

review_comments: In what cases(example code) would we be executing this block?

All cases in  DebuggerTests.EvaluateOnCallFrameTests.EvaluateBrowsableRootHidden because
```
Error Message:
   [] Could not find variable 'listRootHidden[0]'
```
This PR fixes only the problem with `Items` vs `_items` (now it's always `Items`). But it does not fix the fact that they need to get expanded manually - rootHidden info does not exist on them and cannot be easily extracted. The issue where we address it is this one: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/76876.

Is my understanding here correct?:

1. `List<T>` has `[DebuggerTypeProxy(typeof(ICollectionDebugView<>))]`, so we look at the proxy
2. the proxy has `Items` property
3. `Items` has `[DebuggerBrowsable(DebuggerBrowsableState.RootHidden)]`, which isn't working yet (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/76876)
4. So, we are expanding `Items` here to work specifically for `List<T>`?

If so, then is this only to get `EvaluateBrowsableRootHidden` passing?
Also, does https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/76876 still happen after the DebuggerTypeProxy fix here?

I looked at it, and (4) is true. The test for `listRootHidden` should be disabled for now, and a comment mentioning the issue. And we can remove this incorrect hack.
And in a follow up PR, the root hidden issue can be fixed.

I would say it's a misunderstanding caused by me not deleting the dependency on non-fixed values in the tests properly. Manual expansion was not done on an object decorated with `RootHidden` but on `testPropertiesNone`. The `else` block is not to make the tests pass, it is necessary till `RootHidden` on `Items` will be received correctly by Proxy. It was the test that was not 100% logical.
I think now it will make more sense after the last commit.

Yes, the issue is still here. Proxy is not receiving any DebuggerAttributes assigned to `Items`, so it does not know it's of rootHidden type.

> I looked at it, and (4) is true. The test for `listRootHidden` should be disabled for now, and a comment mentioning the issue. And we can remove this incorrect hack. And in a follow up PR, the root hidden issue can be fixed.

Sorry, this comment did not display for me when I was investigating. I don't agree. This will break mechanism for all Collections that are in rootHidden objects. The `else` block can be removed when we have the fix already, so that we won't be changing the behavior from working to not working.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8064bfe0c2b1b90f9922767a4475685722eaeb78/src/mono/wasm/debugger/BrowserDebugProxy/MemberObjectsExplorer.cs#L149-L161

This code is *very explicitly* looking for a `Items` member which is an `array`. So, the `else` arm is affecting only the very specific types that have such a member, which is the case for `List<T>`. The proxy, or the debugger agent aren't populating it as an extra thing.

I agree that we shouldn't break the behavior in this PR. But it *is* incorrect. We want to avoid depending on magic like that, especially when proper mechanisms are available to get the information - `DebuggerTypeProxy` in this case.

The rootHidden issue is in addition to this, and that's fine to fix separately.
